results.title: Neon Pricing: Free Plan With 100 Projects, Typical Spend $15/Month
results.snippet:
Public network transfer is counted per project, not per account:

       Free plan: 5 GB per project per month, across up to 100 projects
       Launch and Scale: 500 GB per project per month, then $0.10 per GB

Each project's allowance is shared by everything in it: Postgres, Object Storage, and Functions. Eligible startups can apply for up to $100k in credits through the Startup Program. Learn how to reduce network transfer.

   ### How do Neon costs scale as I add projects or traffic? [...] Free plan: up to 100 projects at $0, each with its own 100 CU-hours and 1 GB of storage, enough to build and test a database-per-tenant app.
       Launch and Scale: you pay only for the compute each tenant actually runs and the storage it holds. Idle tenant databases scale to zero, so inactive tenants don't add compute cost; storage is still billed. Launch includes 100 projects, and Scale includes 1,000, with more on request. [...] `Monthly CU-hours = [average CU size] × [number of hours the compute runs in the month]``Monthly compute cost = [monthly CU-hours] × [CU-hour price]`
The CU-hour price depends on your pricing plan:

       Launch plan: $0.106 per CU-hour
       Scale plan: $0.222 per CU-hour

Remember that when your database is idle, compute can scale down to zero, so you don't consume CU-hours while it's not running. Learn more about Neon's billing.

results.title: Neon Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs & Limits
results.snippet:
Summarize with AI



Share article



Neon pricing starts with a free plan; paid Launch and Scale plans charge for actual usage with no monthly minimum. Database compute costs $0.106 per CU-hour on Launch and $0.222 on Scale, with storage billed separately. The main budget question is how much compute runs, and for how long—not how many colleagues log in. [...] ## Which plan should you choose?

Use Free while the real workload fits its per-project limits. Move to Launch when storage, compute, or idle behavior requires it. Choose Scale when its controls or capacity are necessary. Measure a representative week—including background jobs—before projecting a full month.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Neon really free?

Yes, within the Free plan allowances. Free is not a time-limited trial; paid resources and higher requirements change the budget. [...] | Plan | Billing | Database allowance or rate | When it fits |
 ---  --- |
| Free | $0; no annual commitment | 100 CU-hours and 0.5 GB storage per project | Experiments and small workloads within every free limit |
| Launch | Usage billed monthly; no fixed annual equivalent | $0.106/CU-hour; $0.35/GB-month | Applications that exceed Free without requiring Scale controls |

results.title: Neon plans - Neon Docs
results.snippet:
Free: No charge, up to 6 hours, limited to 1 GB of change history per project
   Launch: Up to 7 days, billed at $0.20/GB-month
   Scale: Up to 30 days, billed at $0.20/GB-month

You can change your history window to control how much change history you retain for instant restore. See Instant restore for how to use the feature.

> The change history is a log of write operations in the form of Postgres Write-Ahead Logs.

### History window for your project. [...] 0.25 CU for 4 hours = 1 CU-hour
   2 CU for 3 hours = 6 CU-hours
   8 CU for 2 hours = 16 CU-hours

Free: 100 CU-hours/project/month (enough to run a 0.25 CU compute in a project for 400 hours/month).  
Launch: $0.106/CU-hour  
Scale: $0.222/CU-hour

> All computes in your project count toward usage. Each branch has a read-write compute by default; read replicas add read-only computes. [...] ### How are read replicas billed?

Each read replica is its own compute and contributes to CU-hours.

### Do public network transfer limits reset each month?

Yes. Free includes 5 GB per project per month. Launch and Scale include 500 GB per project per month, then $0.10/GB.

### How is private network transfer billed?

Only available on Scale: $0.01/GB, bidirectional, between Neon and private network services.
